description: In repos/goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts, the edit-intent escalation return block grades a goal `reached: false` even when the edit has already landed on origin/dev. The block returns an object containing `selectedTemplateId: "feature_compose"`, `reached: false`, and `executionId: `feature_compose:rejected:${goalHashOf(goal as string)}``, immediately after the tap line that ends `— returning the compose failure`. Before that return, add a last-chance landing check. Compute `const h = goalHashOf(goal as string);` and, for the vessel repo named by the edit file, spawn git in the checkout that tracks origin/dev — the path convention is `/workspace/git/vessels/<vessel>`, as the comment near line 1850 states — using `Bun.spawn` exactly like the existing call at line 10907 does. Run `git log origin/dev -1 --format=%H --grep=route-edit-<h>` and, if it prints a non-empty 40-character sha, return `reached: true` with `status: "completed"`, `executionId: `feature_compose:${sha}``, and a goalReachReason naming the sha as landing evidence; otherwise fall through to the existing `reached: false` return unchanged. Wrap the whole check in try/catch and treat any error or empty output as no landing, so this can only ever turn a false negative into a true positive and never the reverse. This is the same evidence bar the function already applies a few lines earlier, where a landed sha from patch_with_tools is graded `reached:true` — it is a timing fix, not a change to what counts as a reach. Measured cause: the early edit-intent route to feature_compose times out at the caller, the callee lands the commit minutes later, and the verdict has already been written; the compose report at /workspace/proposals/route-edit-<h>-compose-report.json cannot be used as the evidence because a retried attempt overwrites it with rolled_back:true after the successful landing.
